label: TP
reason: Assessed both alerts: Alert 1 (java/xss) shows user input flowing through header->param->doSomething()->bar->fileURI->fileTarget->toString() to the encodeForHTML() sink; however, the encoding mitigates XSS in HTML context. Alert 2 (java/path-injection) is a TRUE POSITIVE: user input from headers flows through the same path to fileTarget, which is used in file system operations (fileTarget.exists()). Path injection allows attackers to control filesystem paths via header parameters, enabling unauthorized file access. At least one alert (path-injection) is confirmed exploitable.

evidence.note: User input from request headers flows through URL decoding, doSomething(), HashMap storage/retrieval, URI construction, and File creation to fileTarget - user controlled data reaches file system operation sink
